comments.author: @tysoncung
comments.text: The part that stopped me: Uzbekistan's state has printed in a reformed Arabic orthography, then Latin in 1929, Cyrillic in 1940, and Latin again in 1992, and in 2026 its parliament was still amending the letters, with Senate changes on 10 September setting out a gradual transition. Kazakhstan's 2017 decree aimed at 2025 and now points to 2031. Sources are linked in the description. If your country changed its script, or its spelling rules, what did it actually change for you at school or at work?

replies.author: @AryssaRiyasat
replies.text: I saw some sources that Qazağystan (my spelling of the nation that reflects real pronunciation) removed deadlines last month because the alphabet needs some fixes.  I’m learning some Kazakh, but because of my young age, I came up with my own Latin alphabet and sound change rules based on common Turkic, and I only ever use Latin to avoid stigma.
